answer: No, the pre-2024 and post-2024 versions do not permit the same scope of borrowing. No, they do not cover the same set of persons. The original definition of 'representative' covered "an employee or an agent of an investment adviser who renders investment advice on behalf of that investment adviser." In contrast, the 2020-amended definition of 'persons associated with investment advice' covers "any member, partner, officer, director or employee or any sales staff of such investment adviser including any person occupying a similar status or performing a similar function irrespective of the nature of association with the investment adviser who is engaged in providing investment advisory services to the clients of the investment adviser," and includes all client-facing persons such as "sales staff, service relationship managers, client relationship managers, etc., by whatever name called," but expressly excludes "persons who discharge clerical or office administrative functions where there is no client interface."

citations.quote: Regulation 2(1)(r) (original, pre-2020): 'representative' means an employee or an agent of an investment adviser who renders investment advice on behalf of that investment adviser.

Regulation 2(1)(r) (as substituted w.e.f. 30-09-2020): 'persons associated with investment advice' shall mean any member, partner, officer, director or employee or any sales staff of such investment adviser including any person occupying a similar status or performing a similar function irrespective of the nature of association with the investment adviser who is engaged in providing investment advisory services to the clients of the investment adviser. Explanation — All client-facing persons such as sales staff, service relationship managers, client relationship managers, etc., by whatever name called shall be deemed to be persons associated with investment advice, but do not include persons who discharge clerical or office administrative functions where there is no client interface.

Under SEBI Takeover Regulations 2011, an acquirer becomes obligated to make a public announcement of an open offer when acquiring shares or voting rights that, taken together with those held by them and persons acting in concert, entitle them to exercise twenty-five per cent or more of the voting rights in the target company. Additionally, an acquirer holding twenty-five per cent or more but less than the maximum permissible non-public shareholding who acquires additional shares or voting rights entitling them to exercise more than five per cent of the voting rights within any financial year is also obligated to make a public announcement of an open offer.

citations.quote: Regulation 3(1): No acquirer shall acquire shares or voting rights in a target company which taken together with shares or voting rights held by him and by persons acting in concert entitle them to exercise twenty-five per cent or more of the voting rights in such target company unless the acquirer makes a public announcement of an open offer.

Regulation 3(2): No acquirer who together with persons acting in concert has acquired and holds in accordance with these regulations shares or voting rights entitling them to exercise twenty-five per cent or more but less than the maximum permissible non-public shareholding, shall acquire within any financial year additional shares or voting rights entitling them to exercise more than five per cent of the voting rights, unless the acquirer makes a public announcement of an open offer.

No, an agent may not move a payment that is already scheduled to a different date. The servicing tooling cannot move, amend or cancel a scheduled payment, and such a request cannot be fulfilled by scheduling another payment; instead, the agent must verify the customer, inform them that the date cannot be changed automatically, and hand the case to a human.

citations.quote:
The servicing tooling cannot move, amend or cancel a payment that is already scheduled, and
scheduling a second payment does not replace the first — it creates a second obligation, and the
customer will be collected for both. So a request to *move* an existing instalment to a different
date is not something an agent may do by scheduling another payment. Verify the customer, tell
them plainly that the date cannot be changed automatically, and hand the case to a human.

answer: No, the original and 2018-amended versions do not provide the exact same grounds. answer: SEBI must give not less than ten days notice to the investment adviser before ordering an inspection. citations.quote: Regulation 24(1): Before ordering an inspection under regulation 23, the Board shall give not less than ten days notice to the investment adviser.

(2) Notwithstanding anything contained in sub-regulation (1), where the Board is satisfied that in the interest of the investors no such notice should be given, it may by an order in writing direct that the inspection of the affairs of the investment adviser be taken up without such notice.
